maria: quick check — i'm wiring sealed-secrets in staging to use our Vault transit key instead of the default rsa. want to make sure i'm not missing an ops step before i flip it on :slightly_smiling_face:
cheng: ah nice. is this for the sealed-secrets controller or the unseal process?
maria: sealed-secrets controller (bitnami). we want to use Vault transit/encrypt to generate the sealed secret payloads so private key material never lives in k8s. plan: controller talks to Vault via Kubernetes auth, uses transit/encrypt-decrypt.
sam: sounds good. any helm/values diff you can paste?
maria: yep, current values i'm testing with — note client TLS and k8s auth role: 
```yaml
replicaCount: 1
controller: 
  env: 
    - name: VAULT_ADDR
      value: https://vault.internal.svc.cluster.local:8200
    - name: VAULT_AUTH_METHOD
      value: kubernetes
  extraArgs: ["--key-type=transit", "--transit-key=secrets/sealed-secrets-key"]
rbac: enabled: true
serviceAccount:
  create: true
  name: sealed-secrets-sa
```
maria: i've created a Vault policy 'sealed-secrets-role' that allows transit/encrypt and decrypt for the key path. i've also bound a k8s service account to the role via the JWT auth role.
cheng: two quick callsouts: 1) ensure Vault response wrapping is off for the transit path, it breaks the controller's unwrap flow. 2) check token TTL — controller expects long lived or renewal. we should use a renewable child token via the k8s auth role.
maria: good call. i set token_ttl = 24h for the role, with max_ttl 168h. is that too short for controller restarts?
sam: 24h should be okay if the controller renews; but if restart happens during revoke window it might fail. i'd prefer 72h default with renew. also make sure we have a fallback key in k8s for emergency unseal (sealed-secrets private key) stored in an encrypted S3 object — ops-bot: created snapshot at s3://redwood-secrets-backups/sealed-secrets/20240614.enc :lock_with_ink_pen:
maria: thanks ops-bot. another question — any network policy or mTLS we need between sealed-secrets and vault? right now vault is in a private ns with a l4 policy allowing kube-system egress.
cheng: you need to allow the sealed-secrets namespace svc account pod selector to talk to vault:8200. if you have istio/mesh, set mTLS permissive for that path first. also, ensure the Vault CA bundle is available to the controller (or use the cluster CA).
maria: ack. i tested locally by port-forwarding and it encrypts, but when controller runs in-cluster it logs 403 on /v1/transit/encrypt/secrets%2Fsealed-secrets-key
sam: 403 implies policy mismatch or wrong token role bound. check the bound service account name on the auth role mount: run `vault read auth/kubernetes/role/sealed-secrets-role` and verify `bound_service_account_names` and `bound_service_account_namespaces`.
maria: i ran that, role shows namespace: staging, service account: sealed-secrets-sa. jwt path matches. policy attached shows capabilities encrypt, decrypt.
cheng: another edge: transit key path encoding — your helm extraArgs used `secrets/sealed-secrets-key`, but controller url-encodes slashes; Vault expects path `transit/keys/secrets/sealed-secrets-key` for key metadata and `transit/encrypt/secrets/sealed-secrets-key` for encrypt. make sure the controller's arg maps correctly. logs often show the final request path.
maria: aha i see the controller request in logs: `POST /v1/transit/encrypt/secrets%2Fsealed-secrets-key` — that should be fine. i compared policies: policy uses `path "transit/encrypt/secrets/*" { capabilities = ["update"] }` — hm the wildcard might not match the encoded slash?
sam: Vault policies match on decoded paths; the wildcard `secrets/*` should match `secrets/sealed-secrets-key`. But if your key is nested more levels you may need `secrets/*` vs `secrets/*/*`. can you try a permissive test policy for that role (`path "transit/encrypt/*" { capabilities = ["update"] }`) and see if 403 goes away?
maria: i'll try that now.
(10 minutes pass)
maria: update — switching to `transit/encrypt/*` fixed it in staging. controller can encrypt/decrypt. i reverted to a narrower policy after confirming exact key path works: `transit/encrypt/secrets/*` — and confirmed controller still works.
cheng: nice. final checklist before promote to prod: 1) add mTLS/CA config to helm values, 2) rotate strategy for transit keys (have a reuse window?), 3) emergency fallback private key in secure backup and tested restore, 4) alerting on controller encryption failures in datadog.
maria: noted. i'll open a small PR with helm chart changes + vault role terraform. pinging @sam for tf review when i have it ready. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: deployment 'sealed-secrets' in staging: rollout started by maria at 1719806000
sam: i'll review the terraform. can you include an example policy + test script? saves time.
maria: will do — thanks all.
